html:
The Kru, a people of the southeastern coast of Liberia, who from the 18th century worked in large numbers as sailors, boatmen and dockworkers on European ships, and were known as Krumen.

They hired on for set terms, then went home with their pay, and were valued for handling surf boats on a coast with few harbours. They worked on British warships of the West Africa Squadron and on trading ships from Senegal to Angola, and built communities in Freetown, Lagos and other ports. A Kru mark tattooed on the forehead showed they were free men, not slaves. In Liberia they resisted Americo-Liberian rule in several wars in the 19th and early 20th centuries.
